items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: I remember he and Alec Stevens got to

ctx.x: Well, I was making money, you see; I was busy making money...and buying cars. But I was in the prime of my life, at that time, It had opened up another whole new avenue that had nothing to do with playing the music. I enjoyed it, I knew... I appreciated it and all that. But it just hadn't gotten to me. It hadn't really affected me in the same way. I enjoyed music. I like it and I liked being around and hearing it. I liked to listen to it and all that.

But I remember Wes was like always the center of attraction. But very likeable, always happy-go-lucky, just... and that's what his music came out like, it was just that force from the energy inside. I remember he and Alec Stevens got to

be very close and they played a lot together, so I'm sure that he had a lot to do with Wes'...the turning point for him, right there, when he come back to Indianapolis and he got in that kind of company, with the amount of total freedom that we both had, different than what we had lived under the roof of my dad. Because with my mother, it was just like a whole new way of life. Great.
